details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for mainly damaging winds is expected to increase from central into eastern Pennsylvania and locations farther east. An additional downstream watch will likely be required

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A transition from a line into more cellular convection has occurred over the past 1-2 hours from the vicinity of an MCV over north-central PA into central PA. Storm mode and poor low-level lapse rates have limited damaging wind potential thus far with the cellular convection. With time, coalescing storm-scale cold pools, 40 kt of westerly deep-layer shear, and continued heating/ destabilization of the inflow air mass should support increasing damaging wind potential from central into eastern PA, and eventually NJ and the lower Hudson Valley. As such, a downstream severe thunderstorm watch will likely be required

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for locally damaging winds is expected to increase this afternoon, likely requiring a severe thunderstorm watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Daytime heating combined with boundary-layer dewpoints in the upper 60s to lower 70s has contributed to a moderately unstable air mass as of early afternoon with steepening low-level lapse rates and MLCAPE of 1500-2500 J/kg. Upstream convection over southwest PA is gradually developing a tighter leading-edge reflectivity gradient and more robust trailing stratiform region, suggestive of an organizing cold pool. Current thinking is that the evolving convective system will further intensify as it continues east-southeast and encounters an increasingly unstable environment across the discussion area. The current KPBZ VWP is sampling strengthening west-northwest flow above 2 km AGL, which will likely aid in further cold pool organization. These factors will lead to an increasing threat for damaging wind gusts across the area this afternoon, likely requiring the issuance of a severe thunderstorm watch

details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of scattered damaging wind gusts will increase while spreading south-southeastward this afternoon. A watch is likely for parts of the area

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Several organized storm clusters are tracking south-southeastward across southeastern OH toward WV. These storms have produced a couple strong wind gusts (50-60 mph). South of this activity, mostly clear skies are promoting ample diurnal heating/destabilization of a moist air mass (lower 70s dewpoints), which combined with steep midlevel lapse rates (sampled by the 12Z ILN sounding), is contributing to moderate surface-based buoyancy. Given the well-established storm clusters/cold pools moving into this environment, and around 30-40 kt of 0-6 km shear (per VWP data) oriented oblique to the leading gust fronts, the risk of scattered damaging wind gusts will continue spreading south-southeastward this afternoon. Instances of severe hail could also occur with the stronger embedded cells. A watch issuance is likely for parts of the area
